evidence: A CODEOWNERS file routes changes to designated reviewers, the repository-side half of enforced change review
expected_output: One observation row with codeowners_present and path

assertions.description: A CODEOWNERS file exists at a location GitHub honors (/, .github/, docs/).

caveats: Proves ownership is declared, not that branch protection enforces it — enforcement lives server-side and needs the GitHub App (appliance phase).

plain.checks: Looks for a CODEOWNERS file in one of the three locations the host honours: the repository root, .github/, or docs/.
plain.violation: Nobody is named as the required reviewer for anything. Review still happens by convention, but nothing routes a change to the people who understand that part of the code, and nothing notices when it does not.
plain.fix: Add a CODEOWNERS file mapping paths to the teams responsible for them, then turn on the branch protection rule that requires their review. The file is the half of this a repository can show; the protection rule is the half that enforces it.
